4.  24-53806  Recommendation to receive and file on the Homeless Count 2024 Presentation
  from Dalton Dorr.

  • The Homeless Count is a HUD requirement and is conducted yearly. This
  year the Count was conducted on January 25th.
  • Data on the Count is provided to give context around what is occurring.
  Determining our progress towards goals and performance and determining
  funding allocations.
  • There are huge changes in numbers from 2022 that shock the system but

  Page 2 of 6
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JUNE 11, 2024
  2000 SAN GABRIEL AVENUE
  CABRILLO GATEWAY CONFERENCE ROOM, 3:00 PM

  that was due to many factors, the pandemic being the main one.
  • In January 2023 the city declared the homelessness emergency declaration,
  the following year we see a 2% decrease in number of people experiencing
  homelessness.
  • Numbers are not changing drastically from one year to the next. One major
  difference this year is that most surveys were conducted at shelters.
  • The increase from last year to this year for those living in their vehicles could
  have been due to the weather conditions during the day of the Count.
  • City staff and board members exchanged conversations about the data
  being presented.
  • This year data shows that less than 50% of people lost their homes in Long
  Beach.
  • City staff and board members exchanged conversations around people in
  shelters and their stability.
  • The costs of rent have doubled over the years, specifically within a 10-year
  period. People are being priced out of the housing market and overall driving
  people into homelessness.
  • No public comment.

  A motion was made by Member Martins, seconded by Member Boyce, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  11 Wee, Shuford, Tan, Topolewski, Washington, Brezenoff, Martins,
  Chotiswatdi, Boyce, McCullom, Diles III
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 8 Weithers, Howat, Pezzelle, Richert, Wilson, Bambrick, Amick,
  McFadzen

5.  24-53807  Recommendation to receive and file the 2024 CoC Updated Polices presentation
  from Alexa Dixson-Griggs.

  • City staff Alexa Dixson-Griggs and Cassandra Bonney from the Health
  Department provided an overview of the 2024 CoC updated policies which
  include, funding priorities, Access Center policy, RRJ Eligibility and
  Prioritization Policy, Matching Procedures, Grievances and Incidents,
  Determining Termination of Assistance, 2024 Written Standards, 2024 Coc
  Charter Bylaws.
  • Access center policy will be applicable to all funding programs not just the
  CoC.
  • Rapid rehousing will have two requirements, one being homeless and
  income. These two will be required to enroll and used to prioritize.
  • City staff and board members had conversations about staffing issues and

  Page 3 of 6
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JUNE 11, 2024
  2000 SAN GABRIEL AVENUE
  CABRILLO GATEWAY CONFERENCE ROOM, 3:00 PM

  rapid rehousing funding.
  • Matching procedures will be matched on a 1:1 scale.
  • Grievances and incidents have updated language across the board. The
  purpose is to provide guidance to providers on reporting requirements.
  Crystal Marin has been hired to oversee grievances.
  • Providers should update current termination policies to reflect changes in
  requirements and contact information, termination policies will need to be
  submitted at the time of funding request.
  • Providers funded through the City of Long Beach should review and update
  P&Ps based on 20024 standards.
  • Some language and terms have changed in the 2024 CoC Governance
  Charter and Bylaws. The HSB team will update the website and calendar
  invites with new subcommittee structures.
  • No public comment.

7.  24-53809  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff and
  Operations Update presentation from Paul Duncan.

  • Quarterly detailed reports will be provided on service numbers, the next one
  will be in August.
  • There was an update on staffing for positions, Alvin Teng has been
  promoted to the City Managers office and will lead a new team under the
  Deputy City Manager Teresa Chandler. Alvin introduced himself to the board
  and provided an overview of his new role. There are additional positions
  going through the interview and background phases.
  • The 2024 Homeless PIT Count report has been released, and there will be a
  press conference to go over the numbers and provide context.
  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan participated in the mayor Rex Richardson
  local, state, and federal leadership meeting addressing youth homelessness.
  • Long Beach presented the 2024 LA Homeless Initiative Symposium on
  encampment resolution and regional partnership approaches.
  • The hotel lease for 2nd encampment resolution went to City Council during
  the June 4th Council meeting. This project will be focused on the Vagabond
  Inn over on 1st and Alamitos, this space has 60 rooms available, and
  programming will start soon.
  • Work project plans are being finalized around merging the Long Beach HMIS
  database with the LAHSA HMIS database.
  • City staff and board members discussed the merging of HMIS database
  further.
  • No public comment.
